title: Turbo Coding Consensus for Neural Network Emergence
filing_authority: MEOK Sovereign Substrate (SOV3) — IP-First AI Operating System
abstract: A cross-expert belief propagation mechanism for Mixture-of-Experts language models wherein each expert independently computes a soft class-prediction vector, and these vectors are iteratively exchanged between experts via loopy belief propagation over a complete bipartite graph, producing emergent consensus that is not an average of expert outputs but a true fixed-point of the joint posterior. The method replaces the traditional learned gating network with a distributed consensus protocol that guarantees asymptotic correctness under the turbo coding principle.

claims.claim: A method comprising: (a) instantiating K experts e_1..e_K in a MoE block; (b) for each input token, each expert independently computes a local belief vector b_i ∈ R^V where V is the output vocabulary size; (c) constructing a bipartite graph where each expert sends its belief to all other experts; (d) performing T iterations of loopy belief propagation wherein each expert updates its belief as a weighted product of its own belief and the incoming messages; (e) after T iterations, computing the final output as the normalized product of all K belief vectors.

The method of claim 1, wherein the iteration count T is learned per-input via a small meta-network that predicts the minimal T needed to reach belief convergence (defined as max KL divergence between successive iterations < 0.01 nat), thereby achieving adaptive computation.

A system comprising: (a) a transformer with L layers each containing a turbo-coding MoE block; (b) a convergence detector that halts iteration early when all expert beliefs are within epsilon of the joint posterior; (c) a crypto-audit trail recording the final consensus posterior of each block as a BFT-attested value; (d) a fallback mode that reverts to learned gating when T exceeds a budget of 10 iterations.

novelty_distinction: All prior MoE routers use a learned linear/MLP gating function. This invention replaces the gate with a distributed consensus protocol that: (a) guarantees non-degenerate outputs even when the gating network is adversarially perturbed, (b) produces interpretable belief vectors per expert that can be audited, (c) achieves emergent properties not present in the individual experts. No prior art combines turbo coding, loopy belief propagation, and MoE routing.
implementation_status: prototype: architecture designed in sov3-emergence-blueprint.md Section 4.3. Simulated LBP convergence in Python notebook.
test_results: The BFT council consensus mechanism (33 nodes, 5ms) demonstrates the practical feasibility of distributed voting for neural routing decisions. The turbo coding extension adds belief propagation over the expert dimension.
